html:
In June 1878 Kanak clans of central New Caledonia rose against French settlers who were taking their land and letting cattle loose on their gardens. The revolt was led by the chief Ataï.

Many settlers were killed in the first attacks. French troops, helped by Kanak clans who were enemies of the rebels, crushed the rising over the following months. Ataï was killed, and his head was sent to Paris; it was only returned in 2014.

Hundreds of Kanak died and whole clans lost their land and were moved. The revolt became a founding memory for the independence movement of Jean-Marie Tjibaou. See French annexation and the penal colony.
